brief.outcome: Raise the share of started checkouts that are completed on the clothing store from 28% to 40% by the end of January 2027, without cutting margin.
brief.deliverable: A rebuilt abandoned-checkout email flow ready in Klaviyo as drafts, a ranked and owner-chosen set of mobile checkout fixes prepared for the owner to apply, and a readout of what moved the completion rate.
done: Funnel numbers checked against real orders, or their limits stated
Payment failures confirmed or ruled out as a cause
Every cause hypothesis marked supported, refuted or unknown with evidence
Owner has chosen the fixes, with reasons recorded
Chosen checkout fixes and email drafts built and checked
Each change applied only with the owner's yes, and registered as a test first
Checkout completion rate read back against the 28% baseline and the 40% target
Learnings saved for the next round

metric.name: Checkout completion rate (checkouts completed as a share of checkouts started)

guardrails: Margin per order does not fall: no new discounts to win checkouts back
Free shipping stays at Rs 999 and above
Add-to-cart rate (about 9% today) does not fall
Abandoned-cart emails do not get more unsubscribes or spam complaints than today
limits: The Rs 999 free-shipping threshold cannot be lowered
Margin cannot be cut to win checkouts
Shopify is connected read-only, so store changes are prepared for the owner to apply
Klaviyo allows read and draft only, so nothing is switched on by us
assets: The existing abandoned-cart email in Klaviyo, not reviewed in a year
unknowns: Whether payment failures are part of the problem, and the failure rate by payment method
Which payment methods the checkout offers today
Completion rate by device, and by new versus returning visitors
What the current abandoned-cart email does, how long ago it was built and how it performs
Order volume, average order value and margin per order
How the 28% figure is defined in Shopify analytics

research.approach: Practitioners treat low checkout completion as a measurement and friction problem before it is an email problem. They split the funnel by step and device, confirm the numbers against real orders, then walk the mobile checkout looking for late-revealed costs, forced sign-up, missing payment methods and payment errors with no retry. Fixes are ranked by impact over effort (guest checkout, early total cost and payment error handling come first), and the recovery email is rebuilt as a separate checkout-started flow with spaced emails and no blanket discount. Each change is tested on its own so the lift can be attributed.

sources.title: Baymard Institute: How to reduce cart abandonment
sources.note: Research-based reasons for abandonment (late costs, forced account, complex checkout, slow delivery) and a fix order by impact and effort, including payment error handling.

sources.title: Attribuly: Shopify abandoned cart recovery checklist 2026
sources.note: Practitioner checklist: check tracking and resume-checkout links first, then a 2 to 3 email sequence (first at 2 to 4 hours, second at 20 to 48 hours), suppress duplicates and use single-use incentives to protect margin.

sources.title: Socio Labs: Shopify checkout optimization, 18 tips
sources.note: Agency write-up for Indian Shopify stores: payment mix (UPI, cards, COD), COD visibility, retry after gateway failure, mobile checkout details. Vendor figures are directional, not proof.

steps.name: Measure the funnel by step and by device
steps.why: Completion rate hides where people leave. Sessions, add to cart, checkout started, payment step and completed, split by mobile and desktop, show which step to work on first.

steps.name: Reconcile funnel counts with real orders
steps.why: The 28% is reported from analytics. Checking completed checkouts against paid orders shows whether the baseline can be trusted.

steps.name: Walk the mobile checkout and check payment methods and errors
steps.why: Missing methods such as UPI or COD, forced sign-up, long forms and failed payments with no retry are the usual leaks, and 80% of this store's traffic is on mobile.

steps.name: Check when shipping cost and the free-shipping rule are shown
steps.why: Costs that appear late are the top reason carts are abandoned. The Rs 999 rule is fixed, so the question is whether shoppers see it and the total early enough.

steps.name: Rank causes by checkouts lost and keep competing explanations
steps.why: Several causes can act at once. Each needs its own fix, and a cause is only worth fixing if the volume lost is large enough.

steps.name: Audit and rebuild the recovery email as a separate checkout flow
steps.why: A year-old flow is likely mistimed. Practitioners split checkout-started from added-to-cart, send early, space follow-ups by at least a day and avoid blanket discounts.

steps.name: Fix in order of impact over effort
steps.why: Easy high-impact items such as showing the total early, guest checkout and payment error handling go before a full checkout redesign.

steps.name: Apply one change at a time and read the result
steps.why: With several changes at once, the lift cannot be attributed and a harmful change can hide behind a good one.

pitfalls.text: Treating cart abandoners and checkout abandoners as one group, so the email is wrong for both.
Trusting vendor percentages (UPI lifts, COD reasons) as if they described this store.
Winning checkouts back with discounts that eat margin.
Skipping payment failures because the owner does not suspect them, when a failed payment often ends the session.
Redesigning the whole checkout before fixing the cheap, high-impact items.

plan.name: Lift checkout completion on mobile without cutting margin

stages.name: Pin down the problem
stages.goal: Turn the owner's words into a measured problem, a target, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Gather the funnel, orders and email data
stages.goal: Pull the last 90 days of funnel steps by device, checkouts and orders with payment status, and the current abandoned-cart flow results into one CSV set in the project.

checks.name: Checkout and order totals match Shopify's own totals for the same dates
Each step is split by mobile and desktop, or the missing split is stated
How Shopify defines checkout started and completed is written down

stages.name: Check the 28% can be trusted
stages.goal: Reconcile completed checkouts with paid orders, and test whether the reported 28% holds on the pulled data and by device. Ends with a verdict on the baseline.

checks.name: Completed checkouts agree with paid orders within 5%, or the gap is explained
The 28% is recomputed from the data and marked VERIFIED, DIFFERENT or UNKNOWN
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for diagnosis

stages.name: Walk the mobile checkout and check payments
stages.goal: Step through the mobile checkout as a shopper: payment methods offered (UPI, cards, COD and others), forced sign-up, form length, when shipping and the Rs 999 rule show, and what happens after a failed payment. Add mobile speed and the gateway's failure data when available.

checks.name: Walked on a phone-sized screen, with every step and screenshot listed
Payment methods offered are listed and compared with what shoppers in India expect
What a shopper sees after a failed payment is recorded, or marked not tested
No real order or payment was placed during the walk

stages.name: Find where the checkouts are lost
stages.goal: Test each hypothesis against the funnel, orders, payment and email data. Rank causes by checkouts lost and keep competing explanations.

checks.name: Every listed hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with evidence
Each finding states the checkouts lost and meets a minimum volume, or is marked low-confidence
Each main finding names a competing explanation
Payment failures are SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN from gateway data, not guessed

stages.name: Rank what to change
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into ranked recommendation cards, easy high-impact items first, each with its effect on margin and how it will be measured.

checks.name: Every card cites the finding it rests on
Every card has expected direction, effort, confidence, risk and how it will be measured
No card cuts margin, adds a discount or changes the Rs 999 rule
Cards are ranked by impact over effort, with measurement fixes first when the funnel check is not CHECKED

stages.name: Owner chooses
stages.goal: The owner picks card IDs. Ask for the reason when they pass on a top card; record it as a decision.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over cards are recorded
A reason is recorded wherever the top card was passed over

stages.name: Prepare the checkout fixes
stages.goal: Prepare the chosen mobile checkout changes as exact steps or ready code for the owner to apply: payment methods and retry, guest checkout, form length, showing the total and the Rs 999 rule early.

checks.name: Only chosen changes are included, each with its before and after
Each change is previewed or comes with exact steps and a way to undo it
No change adds a discount, lowers the Rs 999 threshold or raises a fee

stages.name: Rebuild the recovery emails as drafts
stages.goal: Draft a checkout-started flow and a separate added-to-cart flow in Klaviyo with spaced timing and no blanket discount, so no shopper gets both. Saved as drafts only.

checks.name: Checkout-started and added-to-cart shoppers each enter one flow, never both
Delay before each email is stated, with at least a day between emails
No discount or fee change is promised; free shipping is stated as Rs 999 and above
Everything is saved as drafts and read back, nothing is switched on

stages.name: Owner applies each change
stages.goal: Register each change as a test with its metric and date, then hand the owner one change at a time to apply in Shopify or switch on in Klaviyo. Record what was applied and when.

checks.name: Each change is registered as a test with its date before it is applied
Changes that affect the same step are not applied on the same day
The owner confirms each change is live and we read the result back where we can

stages.name: Read the completion rate honestly
stages.goal: Read the checkout completion rate against the recomputed baseline and the guardrails, by device, after each change.

checks.name: A verdict is given only when enough checkouts were started, otherwise INCONCLUSIVE
Margin per order, add-to-cart rate and unsubscribes are checked
Comparisons use the same definition of completion and the same length of period

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Close each test, record what worked and what did not, propose rules with their scope and plan the next round.

checks.name: Every applied change has a verdict
Each proposed rule says whether it holds for this store, this market or all stores

hypotheses.statement: A large share of started checkouts end in a failed payment with no easy retry.
hypotheses.test: Gateway success and failure rates by payment method, and checkouts that reached the payment step but have no paid order.
hypotheses.confirm_if: A meaningful share of checkouts that reach payment fail on one method or gateway, and many of those shoppers do not come back.
hypotheses.refute_if: Payment success is high on every method and drop-off happens before the payment step.

hypotheses.statement: Shoppers leave because their preferred payment method (UPI, COD or wallet) is missing or hard to find.
hypotheses.test: Payment methods offered against what is expected in India; checkouts lost at the payment step by device.
hypotheses.confirm_if: An expected method is absent or buried, and drop-off at the payment step is high on mobile.
hypotheses.refute_if: All the usual methods are offered and visible and payment-step drop-off is low.

hypotheses.statement: Shipping cost or the Rs 999 free-shipping rule shows too late, so shoppers who are below the threshold leave.
hypotheses.test: Where shipping shows in the flow; completion rate for checkouts below versus above Rs 999.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Completion is clearly lower below Rs 999 and shipping first appears at the last step.
hypotheses.refute_if: Completion is similar above and below the threshold, or shipping is shown on the cart page.

hypotheses.statement: The mobile checkout is slow or long, so mobile shoppers drop out.
hypotheses.test: Completion by device; form fields and steps on mobile; mobile speed on the checkout pages.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Mobile completion is well below desktop and the walk-through finds long forms, forced sign-up or slow pages.
hypotheses.refute_if: Mobile and desktop complete at similar rates and the walk-through is clean.

hypotheses.statement: The year-old abandoned-cart email is mistimed or aimed at the wrong group, so it recovers little.
hypotheses.test: Flow trigger, delay, send volume and orders placed per email; whether checkout and cart shoppers get the same emails.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Late first email, one trigger for both groups or very low recovered orders per send.
hypotheses.refute_if: The flow is split and timed well, and recovered orders are in line with the store's other flows.

hypotheses.statement: The reported 28% is mismeasured, for example by counting test, duplicate or pending checkouts.
hypotheses.test: Recompute completion from checkouts and paid orders for the same dates.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The recomputed rate differs from 28% by more than a few points.
hypotheses.refute_if: The recomputed rate is within a point or two of 28%.

measurement.window: At least 14 days per change, covering two weekends, compared with the recomputed baseline period.
measurement.min_volume: Enough started checkouts per period that a 3-point change is larger than week-to-week noise, to be set once the funnel data is in.
measurement.stop_rule: Stop and roll back a change early only if margin per order, add-to-cart rate or unsubscribes breach their guardrails; otherwise read the full window.
